title: Gravitational filtering, magnetic-field inhomogeneity and Coulomb collisions in a kinetic model of a plasma atmosphere with stochastic heating at its base
authors: Luca Barbieri, Pascal Démoulin, Daniel Verscharen
abstract: We investigate the effects of stochastic heating, magnetic inhomogeneity, and Coulomb collisions in coronal loops using a reduced kinetic model. Coulomb collisions thermalize suprathermal populations generated by intermittent heating and populate velocity-space regions inaccessible from the lower boundary in the collisionless limit. We consider two regimes: when heating varies faster than the electron crossing time, the plasma develops a multitemperature nonthermal distribution; when it varies more slowly than the proton crossing time, individual heated loops approach an isothermal state. In the collisionless limit, conservation of the magnetic moment restricts the accessible velocity space, producing a strong temperature anisotropy, with parallel temperature exceeding perpendicular temperature, and additional density depletion. We find that Coulomb pitch-angle scattering efficiently suppresses these effects under typical coronal conditions. In the short-time-scale regime, density and temperature profiles approach those obtained with a constant magnetic field, while gravitational and collisional filtering sustain the temperature inversion. In the strongly collisional long-time-scale regime, magnetic-field-induced anisotropy is nearly eliminated, and individual loops remain approximately isotropic and isothermal. An increasing temperature profile then emerges only after averaging over unresolved flux tubes with different temperatures. Thus, Coulomb collisions largely suppress the macroscopic kinetic signatures of magnetic-field inhomogeneity in the transition region and low corona.
comments: 24 pages, 2 figures

figs.cap: Comparison of the temperature and density profiles obtained for the different kinetic models considered in this work and in our previous studies [10, 17, 12, 13]. The panels show the parallel temperature $T_{\parallel}$, the perpendicular temperature $T_{\perp}$, the total temperature $T$, and the number density $n$ as functions of height. The four curves show the results of our present model including both Coulomb collisions and magnetic-field inhomogeneity (solid blue), the collisionless model with magnetic-field inhomogeneity (dashed red), the collisional model without field inhomogeneity (dash-dotted green), and the purely collisionless model without field inhomogeneity (dotted purple), as indicated in the legend. The parameters used in the calculation are $n_{0}=2\times 10^{10}\,{\rm cm^{-3}}$, $T_{0}=10^{4}\,{\rm K}$, $d=2\times 10^{3}\,{\rm km}$, and $\Delta T=10^{6}\,{\rm K}$, with the heating-event temperature distribution given by Equation (47).

The same quantities as in Figure 1 are shown, but for the long-time-scale regime, in which the heated population is described by a single Maxwellian. The figure compares the collisional solution with magnetic field inhomogeneity (solid blue curves), the collisionless solution with magnetic field inhomogeneity (dashed red curves), and the collisional constant-cross-section solution (dashed dotted green curves). The parameters adopted in the calculation are the same of Figure 1 apart from $n_{0}=10^{9}\,{\rm cm^{-3}}$, $\hat{T}=10^{6}$ K.

title: Inverse-designed tapers to improve throughput of on-chip astrophotonic spectrographs
authors: Vikram Seenivasan, Pradip Gatkine
abstract: Astrophotonics offers a pathway towards compact and stable spectrographs for future large telescopes. The size of these spectrographs does not scale with the diameter of the telescope aperture; thus, they offer a cost-effective way to achieve astronomy science requirements compared to traditional optical spectrographs. A major limitation of current on-chip astrophotonic spectrographs is the significant loss incurred at interfaces between distinct components, particularly at the input and output fiber interfaces, limiting overall throughput. In this work, we investigate inverse-designed architectures to optimize transitions between these components to improve throughput. Inverse design formulates device design as an optimization problem, enabling non-intuitive geometries that can achieve high performance. We focus on optimizing coupling between an arrayed waveguide grating (AWG) spectrograph and an input single-mode fiber. Our approach explores two classes of fabrication-constrained inverse design. The first is shape optimization, which optimizes the geometry of the boundary of a coupling taper. The second is topology optimization, which optimizes the material distribution in a design region to gradually transform the optical mode between components. Both methods are implemented using the Tidy3D package from Flexcompute. We use germanium-doped silica for the core of the photonic components and silica as the cladding, and we use an SMF-28 fiber as input. This work demonstrates a pathway to improve astrophotonic spectrographs through computational inverse-design methods. Leveraging higher throughput, we can improve signal-to-noise ratios offered by photonic devices and position ourselves to design high-performance, cost-effective instrumentation for the next generation of telescopes, both on the ground and in space.
comments: 9 pages, 12 figures, Proceedings from 2026 SPIE Astronomical Telescopes + Instrumentation Meeting, Conference: Advances in Optical and Mechanical Technologies for Telescopes and Instrumentation VII

title: V347 Aurigae: from Peak to Quiescence
authors: Diya T. Kumar, Lynne A. Hillenbrand, Howard Isaacson
abstract: We present an analysis of eight epochs of high-resolution optical spectra of the YSO (young stellar object) V347 Aur. The source exhibits periodic brightness variations spanning $\sim$2 mag over several months, interpreted as cyclic accretion-burst and quiescent phases, making V347 Aur a useful probe of the broad range of accretion and outflow variability in YSOs. When faint, V347 Aur shows an M-type photospheric absorption spectrum; when bright, it exhibits a strong emission-line spectrum. Our Keck/HIRES spectroscopy was obtained during the decay of an accretion burst. The emission spectrum includes the strong H I, Ca II, and He I transitions commonly seen in YSOs, as well as numerous weaker metal lines, for which we provide a complete inventory. As the star fades, photospheric absorption lines deepen, consistent with decreasing veiling from the accretion continuum. H I and He I emission, which trace accretion, strengthen relative to the continuum as it fades, but show the expected decline in strength with decreasing accretion after correcting for the strong early veiling. Ca II behaves similarly, with line profiles that alternate between red- and blueshifted dominance, which we interpret as the rotation of the magnetospheric accretion flows. Narrow, slightly blueshifted absorption in Ca II, Na I, and K I indicates disk winds with localized density enhancements. Forbidden [O I] and [S II] emission is blueshifted, with broad shoulders and low- and high-velocity narrow peaks, consistent with a disk geometry that obscures much of the receding outflow. Their behavior as the continuum fades is similar to that of the broad accretion lines. The V347 Aur system is a useful proxy both for the ubiquitous short-term accretion variability observed in YSOs, and for their secular evolution on longer time scales.
comments: accepted to PASP

figs.cap: Light curve for V347 Aur obtained from the ATLAS survey [39]. Photometry is in the “orange” band spanning 560-820 nm. Dashed lines mark the dates on which the Keck/HIRES spectra were collected. For ease of comparison, the line colors are consistent with those used in the spectral plots presented below.

Spectra normalized to the continuum in the 7070-7160 Å region, showing the emergence of broad absorption features from TiO as the star V347 Aur fades from an accretion burst. The earlier spectra towards the bottom of the figure (e.g., 2021-11-19, 2021-11-24) show a veiled continuum with minimal to no absorption and weak emission lines, consistent with strong accretion activity. In contrast, later spectra towards the top of the figure (e.g., 2022-01-08, 2022-02-16) exhibit deep photospheric absorption features, reflecting the decreasing veiling as accretion subsides.

Li I 6707.856 Å line normalized to continuum (top row), presented as observed (left) and on a velocity scale (right). Equivalent widths (bottom row) are presented as measured (left) and veiling corrected (right) with error propagation. The corrected equivalent width at 2021-12-17 is set to zero, since the measured value was close to zero but formally negative during this epoch of photometric re-brightening. The legend includes the number of days since peak brightness. As the source fades, the veiling decreases, and the line absorption deepens.

Spectra around the H-alpha line at 6562.80 Å (top), H-gamma at 4340.50 Å (middle), and H-delta at 4101.70 Å (bottom). Left panels show observed, continuum-normalized spectra while middle panels are velocity plots where we omit the last spectrum in the H-gamma and H-delta plots due to noise in the continuum. The right panels show equivalent widths; open circles denote the measured values, while filled circles (connected by a dashed line) denote the veiling-corrected values. For visual clarity, the measured (open) equivalent width measurements at later epochs have been offset by 0.05 magnitudes to avoid overlapping error bars with their veiling-corrected (filled) counterparts. As the star fades over time, the spectral lines become broader with enhanced blue-side emission. In addition, some peaks change their morphology into multiple peaks, especially in H-alpha, or are seen to shift in the location of their peaks, for H-gamma and H-delta. The observed line profiles relative to the continuum level generally increase as the star fades, but the veiling-corrected equivalent widths illustrate that the line strengths are actually decreasing.

Spectra and equivalent width measurements of the CaII line centered at 3968.47 Å (top panels) and 3933.660 Å (bottom panels), similar to Figure 4. As the star fades, the CaII lines become stronger in terms of line-to-continuum, except in the last spectrum. The veiling-corrected equivalent widths show a general correlation between source brightness and line strength.

Spectra and equivalent widths for the He I 5875.65 Å line (top) and the 6678.15 Å line (bottom), similar to Figure 4. In general, as the star fades the He I 5875.65 Å line becomes stronger relative to the continuum, and more sharply peaked. The HeI 6678.15 Å profile initially follows this behavior, but then likely becomes influenced by the FeI that contributes at this same wavelength. The veiling-corrected line strengths decrease over time as the source fades.

title: Mid-infrared Imaging of SR 12 c with JWST/MIRI: Grain Growth in an Evolved Circumplanetary Disk
authors: Ya-Lin Wu, Claire O. Finley, Brendan P. Bowler, Ning Chen, Yuhiko Aoyama, Gregory J. Herczeg, Catherine C. Espaillat, William Best, Ian Czekala, Katherine B. Follette, Adam L. Kraus, Raquel A. Martinez, Connor E. Robinson, Quang H. Tran, Kimberly Ward-Duong, Yifan Zhou
abstract: The physical properties of circumplanetary disks offer insights into the formation of giant planets and their satellites. The circumbinary planetary-mass companion SR 12 c (1200 au from SR 12 AB) hosts an isolated dust disk directly detected with ALMA. We present JWST/MIRI imaging of SR 12 c from 5.6 to 21 $\mu$m and analyze its spectral energy distribution from infrared to submillimeter wavelengths. Phenomenologically, the dust disk can be described by a two-component blackbody with large contrasts in characteristic temperatures and radii. Physically motivated models with varied geometries and heating mechanisms suggest a predominantly flat, irradiation-heated disk with a smaller contribution from viscous dissipation. The disk is inferred to be compact, with an inner radius of ~3 $R_{\rm Jup}$. The outer radius is only loosely constrained, with a characteristic value of ~3 au. The lack of strong 10 $\mu$m excess emission suggests significant grain growth and dust settling. We also find that SR 12 c is broadly consistent with the empirical star-disk scaling relations, providing context for its possible formation pathway. These results demonstrate the power of combining mid-infrared and submillimeter observations with disk modeling to better understand the physical properties of circumplanetary disks.
comments: Published in ApJ

figs.cap: JWST MIRI images of the SR 12 system on a logarithmic scale. SR 12 c is located 8$\farcs$7 southeast of the unresolved binary SR 12 AB. North is up and east is left.

SED fitting of SR 12 c with analytic models. The best-fit model (posterior median) is in blue, the photosphere is in gray, and their sum is in black. The gray shaded band is the 95% posterior predictive interval. The JWST and ALMA measurements are shown in orange. The SR 12 c disk is well described by a two-temperature blackbody (upper left), as well as the irradiated flat-disk model (upper right). The irradiated flared-disk model (middle left) overpredicts the disk flux at $\gtrsim$10 µm because the outer regions would intercept more energy. The viscous-heating-only model (middle right) can reproduce the data, but it requires an accretion rate that is much higher than the observed value of $\sim10^{-11}~M_{\odot}$ yr$^{-1}$. The composite model of irradiation and viscous heating can reproduce the overall SED (bottom left), but the accretion rate is not meaningfully constrained because its posterior distribution accumulates at the lower prior bound (bottom right). This suggests that the observed SED is governed by irradiation, with viscous heating playing a minor role.
The energy flux ratio between irradiation and viscous heating, calculated using Equations (2) and (4). The light and dark gray bands are the 68% and 95% credible intervals, respectively.

The weak 10 µm excess of SR 12 c. We perform a linear regression on the MIRI data points, excluding the F1000W flux density. The red and blue belts represent the 68% and 95% credible intervals, respectively. The F1000W measurement is 1.1 times higher than the predicted continuum (2.35 versus $2.12\times 10^{-18}$ erg s$^{-1}$ cm$^{-2}$ Å), indicating a weak excess of silicate emission.

title: The Impact of an AGN on PAH Spectral Features in Galaxy Evolution Simulations: Continuum Dilution and Excitation of PAHs
authors: Grant P. Donnelly, Desika Narayanan, Paul Torrey, J. -D. T. Smith, Helena M. Richie, Hui Li, Federico Marinacci
abstract: Galaxies hosting an active galactic nucleus (AGN) show diminished power and non-standard spectral feature ratios from polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) compared with normal star-forming galaxies. Proposed mechanisms for this difference include a combination of AGN-driven PAH grain processing, differential heating from the surrounding radiation field, and continuum dilution. These potentially competing factors are difficult to disentangle observationally. In this paper, we investigate the impact of the AGN radiation field on the excitation properties and potential dilution of the mid-IR emission features via constrained numerical experiments of idealized galaxies in simulations that include a self-consistent model for the evolution of dust. We find that, for the integrated spectrum of our simulated Milky Way analog and independent of grain-processing physics, the apparent PAH emission is progressively diminished as AGN luminosity is increased. For spectra within the central half kiloparsec, PAH features are entirely obfuscated when an AGN of any sampled luminosity is present. We additionally find that the UV radiation from an AGN is capable of impacting PAH band ratios, though note that we do not yet include a model for potential photodestruction of PAHs. Our model suggests that the inferred lack of PAHs via featureless mid-IR spectra from galaxies hosting AGN may simply owe to the direct continuum from the AGN overpowering mid-IR features from PAHs in the ISM of the host galaxy. Future work will investigate the relative role of AGN continuum dilution and PAH heating vs photodestruction/ionization of PAHs.
comments: Submitted to ApJ. 13 pages, 8 figures

figs.cap: Example decomposed global SED for the simulated galaxy with a realistic PAH mass fraction ($q_{\mathrm{PAH}}\approx 6\%$ at $t=2\,\mathrm{Gyr}$) with a moderate-luminosity AGN ($\eta=0.01$). The black line is the total SED including all luminous sources after the radiative transfer, including the AGN, and the red line shows the PAH-only spectrum after radiative transfer. The blue line is the unattenuated [19] template AGN SED scaled to the present AGN luminosity. The SED for the same galaxy snapshot, but with no AGN ($\eta=0$), is shown as the black dashed line. Note that the PAHs have been noticeably diluted in the total SED when the AGN is present.

Interstellar radiation fields incident on dust grains for different values of $\eta$, integrated within the region $r<0.5\,\mathrm{kpc}$ for the galaxy at $t=9\,\mathrm{Gyr}$ (left panel), and the region $r<20\,\mathrm{kpc}$, which contains most of the simulated galaxy, for the galaxy at $t=2\,\mathrm{Gyr}$ (right panel). The AGN SED becomes the dominant part of the galaxy SED even at moderate $\eta$.

A subset of the MIR spectra extracted from our simulated galaxy with different AGN luminosity scale factors $\eta$ at $r<0.5\,\mathrm{kpc}$ (and $t=9\,\mathrm{Gyr}$) and $r<20\,\mathrm{kpc}$ (and $t=2\,\mathrm{Gyr}$) for the left and right panels, respectively. Different colors represent the different POWDERDAY runs with different values of $\eta$. At low $\eta$, PAH spectra are prominent, but are reduced in prominence as the AGN luminosity increases.

Each curve represents the fractional change in the EQW, relative to the $\eta=0$ POWDERDAY run (no AGN), for different PAH features as $\eta$ increases. The PAH features have been integrated over $r<20\,\mathrm{kpc}$ for the $t=9\,\mathrm{Gyr}$ simulation state, which has a more even distribution of PAHs across radii. The increased impact of dilution from the AGN continuum lowers the PAH EQW as the relative AGN luminosity increases. The $17\,\mathrm{\mu m}$ PAH feature is particularly affected by continuum dilution, and the negative EQW results from the increased curvature of the ${\sim}17\,\mathrm{\mu m}$ continuum at intermediate $\eta$.

Integrated PAH luminosity within annuli for runs with $\eta>0$, normalized by the run with $\eta=0$ (no AGN), as a function of radius from the $t=9\,\mathrm{Gyr}$ galaxy center. Thus, we show the increase in PAH brightness at different radii due to photons received from the AGN. In our experiment, the AGN can contribute significantly to PAH heating even at large radii. The curves converge at small radii because of the cap of the ISRF intensity (at $\mathrm{log}\,U=2$, see Appendix A) under the SPA.

Comparison of short-to-long (STL) wavelength PAH band ratios resulting from $\eta=1$ and $\eta=0$ as a function of radius in the $t=9\,\mathrm{Gyr}$ galaxy. Data points are ratios of PAH features from PAHFIT, and lines are the data smoothed with a moving average of five data points. STL ratios are sensitive to PAH temperature, where higher STL ratios indicate hotter grains. The STL ratios tend to rise as regions approach the nucleus, showing how the AGN radiation increases the average temperature of PAH grains.

title: Long-term ultraviolet variability of Taurus T Tauri stars from the IUE archive
authors: Ana I Gomez de Castro
abstract: Ultraviolet (UV) radiation from Classical T Tauri stars, generated primarily by magnetospheric accretion, plays a fundamental role in circumstellar disk evolution. However, its long-term variability remains poorly characterized due to the scarcity of homogeneous time-series observations. We investigate the variability of the near-UV continuum and the Mg II resonance doublet to assess whether both diagnostics trace the same underlying accretion variability. We analyzed the complete archive of long-wavelength International Ultraviolet Explorer (IUE) observations of T Tauri stars in Taurus-Auriga, comprising 475 low-dispersion spectra of 36 objects collected over 18 years. We characterized continuum variability using three windows between 2600 and 3100 Angstroms and examined continuum-subtracted Mg II fluxes, UV-V colors, and Lomb-Scargle periodograms to investigate correlations and characteristic timescales. Continuum fluxes between 2675 and 3055 Angstroms are strongly correlated, with variability dominated by changes in continuum level rather than spectral shape. Near-UV and quasi-simultaneous optical fluxes are significantly correlated in six of the seven best-sampled sources, although their relative variability differs. The Mg II-continuum relationship shows substantial object-to-object diversity, ranging from correlated variations with different fractional responses to decoupled or anti-correlated behavior, indicating no universal temporal response. Lomb-Scargle periodograms reveal formally significant features in some well-sampled objects, including near 10 and 33 days. However, irregular and clustered sampling prevents their identification as reliable periodic or characteristic timescales.
comments: A&A accepted, 12 figures

title: An Enhanced Intersecting-Lines Method for Optical Loss Characterization in SIS Heterodyne Receivers
authors: François Joint, Magnus Strandberg, Denis Meledin, Igor Lapkin, Sven-Erik Ferm, Mathias Fredrixon, Leif Helldner, Alexei Pavolotsky, Erik Sundin, Victor Belitsky, Vincent Desmaris
abstract: Accurate knowledge of radio-frequency (RF) losses in front of superconductor--insulator--superconductor (SIS) mixers is essential for optimizing millimeter- and terahertz heterodyne receivers. However, such losses are difficult to extract from conventional hot/cold-load measurements because the measured receiver noise combines contributions from the input optics, the mixer, and the intermediate-frequency chain. In this work, we present a numerical implementation of the straight-line, or intersecting-lines, method for estimating input-referred RF noise and optical loss from standard Y-factor measurements. Hot/cold IF spectra are acquired while sweeping the local oscillator (LO) pumping level from under-pumped to over-pumped operation, so that each IF frequency bin gives a family of linear relations between receiver output power and input load temperature. We evaluate all pairwise intersections between these lines and analyze the crossing cloud to obtain the effective RF input noise. We repeat the analysis across the IF band and multiple LO tunings which provides a frequency-resolved characterisation of the input losses over the full band. Our implementation turns the straight-line technique into a reproducible framework for receiver characterisation and relative optical-loss comparison in low-loss front-end configurations.

title: Impact of Residual Gain Errors on the Detectability of Ionized Bubbles during Reionization with SKA 21-cm observations
authors: Arnab Mishra, Kanan K. Datta, Iffat Nasreen, Snehasish Saha, Sk. Saiyad Ali
abstract: Detecting ionized bubbles and characterizing their properties and the surrounding intergalactic medium (IGM) using the HI 21-cm signal provides direct probes of cosmic reionization. Here, we focus on the detection of individual ionized bubbles around luminous sources using a matched-filter technique. We investigate the impact of time- and frequency-correlated residual antenna gain errors on the detectability and characterization of individual ionized regions with SKA-Low. We simulate mock SKA-Low AA* observations that include the HI 21-cm signal, astrophysical foregrounds, residual gain errors, and system noise corresponding to 100 h of observing time. We subtract the foreground components from the gain-corrupted data and subsequently apply the matched-filter technique to the residual visibilities. We find that the matched-filter technique is able to detect the ionized bubble and constrain its properties in the presence of residual gain errors with the rms amplitudes up to $\sigma_A\sim1\%$ and rms phases up to $\sigma_\phi\sim1^\circ$. Residual gain errors at similar levels prevent the reliable identification of ionized regions in reconstructed HI 21-cm images and bias the estimated HI 21-cm power spectrum. Furthermore, we find that increasing the temporal correlation length increases the level of gain-induced artifacts in the reconstructed image. In contrast, increasing the frequency correlation length reduces these artifacts, as some fraction of the spectrally smooth gain-induced residuals is removed during foreground subtraction. We further find that the inferred bubble and IGM parameters remain largely unaffected by residual gain errors, although their uncertainties can increase. These results demonstrate the potential and robustness of the matched-filter technique for detecting and characterizing individual ionized bubbles in the presence of substantial residual calibration errors.

title: Tidal Disruption Events in Active Galactic Nuclei: Thermal Radiation and Jets
authors: Nimrod Tripto, Tsvi Piran, Julian Krolik
abstract: Over the past decade, dozens of Tidal Disruption Events (TDEs) have been identified, with many more expected from upcoming surveys. A small subset has been observed to launch transient, highly luminous relativistic jets, for which the origin of the requisite magnetic flux has not been identified. A non-negligible fraction of TDEs are expected in Active Galactic Nuclei (AGNs), where a magnetized accretion flow is already present. As shown first by Chan et al. (2019), the collision of a TDE debris stream with this flow can substantially alter both disk and debris dynamics, leading to a possibly Eddington-limited flare. Here, we use the Athena++ radiation magnetohydrodynamic (RMHD) code to simulate the time near peak fallback rate of a TDE in an AGN, studying the debris-disk interaction, the radiation emitted, and the accumulation of magnetic flux near the horizon. In the example simulated, the accretion rate climbs to $\sim 12\,\dot{M}_{ \rm Edd}$, while the escaping solid angle-integrated luminosity approaches $\sim L_{ \rm Edd}$. The photon luminosity is strongly asymmetric, brighter in the hemisphere from which the debris strikes the disk and dimmer in the hemisphere toward which the debris travels. The photon spectrum peaks in the EUV. The polar magnetic flux grows $\sim 33$-fold, enough to raise the Blandford--Znajek luminosity by a factor $\sim 10^3$, reaching a level sufficient to power observed TDE jets. The polar magnetic flux is also asymmetric, likely making any jet similarly asymmetric, but in the opposite sense to the photon flux.
comments: 16 figures, 1 table. Submitted to ApJ

figs.cap: Three orthogonal cuts through the domain showing density slices and velocity streamlines at three epochs. The top row shows the initial disk prior to stream injection, while the middle and bottom rows show the flow after the stream-disk collision has driven strong asymmetries, spiral shocks, tilting and thickening of the disk, and partial evacuation of the inner disk. Times are labeled in units of orbits at $15r_{\rm g}$. The dotted cyan curves mark the thermalization photosphere, defined by $\tau_{\rm eff}=\sqrt{\tau_{\rm abs}(\tau_{\rm abs}+\tau_{\rm sc})}=1$, and the dashed white curve marks the scattering photosphere from the Rosseland-mean optical depth; both are integrated inward from the outermost $z$ in the domain. After stream injection, the south photosphere lies below this $r=30\,r_{\rm g}$ frame; both surfaces are shown on a larger scale in Fig. 4. Full video available here.

(Top) Disk surface density $\Sigma_{\rm disk}=\int\rho\,dz$ limited to $\theta\in[5\pi/16,11\pi/16]$ to include only disk matter, with outgoing stream matter removed by masking elements with $\rho>3\cdot 10^{-11}\,\text{g}\,\text{cm}^{-3}$ and either $|v_{\phi}|/c<3\cdot 10^{-2}$ or the combination $|v_{\phi}|/c<10^{-1}$ and $|v_{\theta}|/c>5\cdot 10^{-2}$. At $t=0$ the disk shows low-amplitude fluctuations. By $4.91$–$10.62t_{\rm orb}$ the stream impact opens a cavity elongated along the rotation direction while the inner disk density grows as matter drains inward; both features partially smooth out as additional matter enters the outer disk. By $23.45t_{\rm orb}$ the cavity has smoothed over and $\Sigma_{\rm disk}$ rises gradually outward, leaving only a faint spiral arm near $r\sim 15r_{\rm g}$ trailed by an under-dense lane. This lane grows more pronounced through $35.53t_{\rm orb}$ as the surrounding disk density continues to grow ($\Sigma_{\rm disk}>10^{3}\,{\rm g\,cm^{-2}}$ outside $r\sim 10r_{\rm g}$), and by $43.50t_{\rm orb}$ the disk has relaxed to a smooth, nearly axisymmetric high-density state with only the lane persisting. The outer disk is supplied by stream material that has gained angular momentum, as shown in Fig. 7. (Bottom) Azimuthally averaged $\langle\Sigma_{\rm disk}\rangle_{\phi}$ vs. $r/r_{\rm g}$ for the same epochs. At $t=0$, the profile is empty inside the ISCO and peaks near $r\sim 10$–$12r_{\rm g}$. Following stream impact, the peak shifts inward and sharpens ($4.91$–$10.62t_{\rm orb}$) as matter piles up in the inner region, then flattens as the disk relaxes ($23.45$–$43.50t_{\rm orb}$); by $t=43.50t_{\rm orb}$ the profile rises nearly monotonically from $r\sim 5r_{\rm g}$ outward. Full video available here.

Meridional density slices at $t=15.35\,t_{\rm orb}$, the same epoch as the middle row of Fig. 2, now extending to $|x|,|z|\sim 700\,r_{\rm g}$ so that both photospheres are visible. Top: $\phi=1.52$; bottom: $\phi=3.14$. Curves as in Fig. 2: dotted cyan, thermalization photosphere ($\tau_{\rm eff}=1$); dashed white, scattering photosphere. The south photosphere follows the outgoing stream to $|z|\simeq 200{-}600\,r_{\rm g}$.

The dynamical response of the disk as a function of time (bottom axis in orbits at $15\,r_{\rm g}$; top axis in days). Grey markers throughout indicate the epochs shown in other figures. (a) $\dot{M}$ in Eddington units at $r=4\,r_{\rm g}$ and $r=30\,r_{\rm g}$ (the unperturbed disk has $\dot{M}=0.07\dot{M}_{\rm Edd}$). The stream-disk interaction drives a sustained rise of $\dot{M}$ to $\simeq 10$–$13\,\dot{M}_{\rm Edd}$ at both radii. (b) Enclosed disk mass within $r<12\,r_{\rm g}$ and $r<30\,r_{\rm g}$. Inside both these radii, $M_{\rm enc}$ eventually increases by a factor $\simeq 5$. While the inner mass reaches a plateau, the outer mass continues to increase. (c) North ($\theta\in[0,\pi/4]$, yellow dashed) and south ($\theta\in[3\pi/4,\pi]$, pink dashed) polar-cap magnetic flux, $\Phi=r^{2}\int_{0}^{2\pi}d\phi\,\int_{\theta_{1}}^{\theta_{2}}B_{r}\,\sin\theta d\theta$, before and after stream injection. The mean flux (blue) and its smoothed trend (black) are shown. Pre-impact $\Phi\simeq 6\cdot 10^{27}\,\mathrm{G\,cm^{2}}$ is flat; after impact the mean rises by a factor $\simeq 4$ within $1$–$3$ orbits, and the south reaches $\simeq 2\cdot 10^{29}\,\mathrm{G\,cm^{2}}$ by $\sim 3$ d, exceeding the north by a factor $\sim 3$. (d) North (yellow) and south (pink) bolometric luminosities, obtained by integrating the vertical flux $F_{z}$ over the sky-plane footprint of the scattering photosphere, as seen along the $z$ line of sight (Figs. 2 and 4). After impact, the thermally photon-bright north side rises toward $\sim L_{\rm Edd}$; the south declines after an initial bump because the outgoing stream obscures photons and carries them with it.

Density as a function of $\theta$ and $\phi$ on three spherical shells, $r=6$, $10$, and $20\,r_{\rm g}$ (left to right), shown at three epochs (top to bottom). At $t=0$ the gas lies in a thin, axisymmetric equatorial layer that is nearly absent at $r=6\,r_{\rm g}$ and becomes denser toward $r=20\,r_{\rm g}$. After stream injection, a vertically oscillating stream wraps in $\phi$ and produces a flow tilted with respect to the equatorial plane that persists to late times; the stream is most coherent at small $r$ and becomes broader, more turbulent, and clumpy at $r=20\,r_{\rm g}$.

Radiation and magnetic fields on two meridional slices at $t=15.35\,t_{\rm orb}$. (Top) Radiation temperature $T_{\rm rad}=(E_{\rm rad}/a)^{1/4}$ (background) and radiation flux streamlines, colored by the isotropic-equivalent luminosity $L_{\rm iso}=4\pi r^{2}(\mathbf{F}_{\rm rad}\cdot\hat{r})$, ranging from $\simeq 10^{44}$ to $\simeq 10^{46}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$, at $t=15.35\,t_{\rm orb}$. Inward-going streamlines are colored gray, since $L_{\rm iso}$ is negative for them. Near the midplane $\tau\gg 1$, so $\mathbf{F}_{\rm rad}$ is parallel to the flow. In the northern hemisphere, the photosphere is at a few $r_{\rm g}$ above the disk. Above it, the flux turns outward and escapes. However, the photosphere in the southern hemisphere lies beyond the range of this plot; hence, some of the flux is directed inwards, and even the flux lines directed outwards are trapped. (Bottom) Density (background) with magnetic-field streamlines. Away from the midplane, the field structure near the inner boundary is nearly monopolar, with field lines pointing toward the black hole. This coherent structure could create strong jets. Flux in the southern hemisphere is $\times$few larger than in the northern one, so jets, if produced, would be $\times$10 stronger in the south.

title: A 4-20 GHz Superconducting 90deg Hybrid Using Capacitively Loaded Coupled Lines for 2SB Heterodyne Receivers
authors: François Joint, Max Behrens, Denis Meledin, Cristian Lopez, Magnus Strandberg, Sven-Erik Ferm, Mathias Fredrixon, Leif Helldner, Alexei Pavolotsky, Erik Sundin, Igor Lapkin, Victor Belitsky, Vincent Desmaris
abstract: We report the design and cryogenic characterisation of a broadband superconducting 90deg intermediate-frequency (IF) hybrid covering 4 to 20 GHz for sideband-separating (2SB) heterodyne receivers. The hybrid is implemented in thin-film niobium using capacitively loaded edge coupled transmission lines, avoiding the air-bridge interconnections required in Lange-coupler layouts while retaining a compact superconducting implementation with low loss and good quadrature balance. Cryogenic measurements using Vector Network Analyser (VNA) show amplitude and phase imbalance better than 0.6 dB and 6deg, respectively, across the full band. When used in a 2SB receiver, this level of IF balance is consistent with the observed image-rejection performance in the 10-20 dB range, for the full receiver. The design supports the development of wide-instantaneous-bandwidth 2SB receivers for millimeter and submillimeter observatories, improving spectral grasp for broadband line surveys and high-redshift line searches.

title: Single-Transit Parameter Estimation with Calibrated Uncertainties
authors: Helem Salinas, Rafael Brahm, Greg Olmschenk, Melinda Soares-Furtado, Karim Pichara, Joshua E. Schlieder
abstract: The growing volume of photometric data from current and upcoming exoplanet surveys demands automated analysis pipelines to detect and characterize exoplanet transit signals. Among these, single-transit events present a challenge, since only one event is observed, and standard transit-fitting techniques for periodic signals do not directly apply because they rely on phase-folding. Beyond detection, characterizing these events is equally critical for follow-up, yet existing approaches are either sensitive to stellar variability and require prior detrending, or depend on stellar priors and per-target fitting. This work presents a convolutional neural network that predicts transit depth, duration, and mid-transit time, together with calibrated uncertainties, directly from a single transit signal. Our network is trained on synthetic light curves and evaluated against a trapezoidal least-squares baseline. On 120 confirmed exoplanets, both methods achieve comparable median errors, but the baseline fails to locate the transit in 10% of cases, producing unreliable estimates that would propagate into follow-up prioritization. In contrast, our network fails in only 1% of cases, yields lower mean absolute errors, and does not require detrending or stellar priors. Detrending would distort or remove the transit along with high stellar variability, precisely where the baseline fails and our network succeeds. Finally, we identify 169 new transit candidates in TESS Sectors 27-60 and apply our approach to obtain their physical parameters, creating a catalog that includes single-transit, multi-transit and multi-planet systems. This approach offers a scalable path toward automated characterization of single transit events, a population that will grow with upcoming surveys.

figs.cap: An overview of the architecture of the CNN used in this work for transit parameter estimation. The network passes input LC through a four-layer 1D convolutional network. For depth, we use average pooling, while for duration, we concatenate average and standard deviation pooling. For mid-transit time, the feature map passes directly to a SoftArgmax head. For each parameter, the network predicts $\mu$ and the log-uncertainty $\log{\sigma}$.

title: The Star Formation Histories of Different Components of M31's Halo from Photometric Estimates of Fe and $α$ Abundances
authors: Jihye Hong, Evan Kirby, Roman Gerasimov, Masashi Chiba, Yutaka Komiyama, Itsuki Ogami, Tiffany Tang, Timothy Beers, Young Sun Lee
abstract: We present the chemical-abundance distributions and star-formation histories of the M31 halo components using photometric Fe and $\alpha$ abundance estimates derived from the PAndAS broad-band $g$ and $i$ filters and the Subaru/HSC $NB515$ narrow-band filter. We selected about 76,400 candidate M31 giant stars and constructed a synthetic photometric training dataset based on model isochrones. We estimated elemental abundances and errors using random forest regression models. We identify various halo components, including about 32,500 stars in the ``smooth" halo (where ``smooth" refers to the complete sample with all the known substructures removed), and infer their star-formation histories from comparisons of their abundance distributions. From the radial abundance gradients, we find that [Fe/H] decreases while [$\alpha$/Fe] increases toward the outer halo. Including substructures further enhances the radial abundance contrast, suggesting that the smooth halo stars are accreted at relatively early times, before the progenitor galaxies produce large numbers of Type Ia supernovae. Both M31 and the Milky Way show similar radial gradient trends, but M31 exhibits higher [Fe/H] and lower [$\alpha$/Fe] values overall, suggesting that the smooth halo of M31 may possess a larger fraction of relatively younger stars associated with more recent merger events. Future photometric observations with additional narrow-band filters and larger spectroscopic samples are expected to provide a better understanding of the formation and evolution history of M31.

title: Simulations of Particle Acceleration by an Interplanetary Shock Observed at 0.07 au and 0.7 au
authors: F.-J. Kong, G. Qin, Y. Wang
abstract: Parker Solar Probe (PSP) observed a coronal mass ejection (CME)-driven shock at 0.07 au on 2022 September 5, and the same CME-driven interplanetary shock was subsequently observed by Solar Orbiter (SolO) at 0.7 au on 2022 September 6. Such a large difference in heliocentric distance between the two shock events enables our comparative study of particle acceleration in near-Sun and far-Sun regions. Using a backward-in-time test-particle approach in a slab-2D turbulent magnetic field model, we perform particle acceleration simulations for the 0.07 au PSP shock and 0.7 au SolO shock, covering the energy ranges measured by PSP/EPI-Lo (0.0697-8.06 MeV) and SolO/EPD (0.0495-5.83 MeV). With an initial kappa = 3 kappa distribution, the particle fluxes at the shock passage are successfully reproduced using effective local shock angles of 70 degrees for the PSP shock and 80 degrees for the SolO shock. Both the observed and simulated energy spectra exhibit a double power-law form. The 0.07 au PSP spectrum softens above 0.75 MeV, while the 0.7 au SolO spectrum hardens slightly above 0.51 MeV, revealing distinct near-Sun and far-Sun acceleration environments. Compared with the observations, the simulations yield harder energy spectra with higher break energies of 2 MeV at 0.07 au and 3 MeV at 0.7 au, indicating efficient particle acceleration under the initial kappa = 3 distribution. Both the observed and simulated spectral indices are harder than the standard diffusive shock acceleration (DSA) prediction, likely arising from non-local acceleration at the large-angle quasi-perpendicular shocks, efficient injection of pre-accelerated suprathermal particles, and the finite shock lifetime effect.

title: Spectroscopic Studies of Meteors within the Skytinel Network
authors: Ernest Świerczyński, Mateusz Żmija, Paweł Zaręba, Tomasz Żywczak
abstract: We present 12 low-resolution meteor spectra recorded at four stations of the Skytinel network in Poland, focusing on consistent reduction and comparison of Fe, Mg, and Na emission features. Spectra spanning approximately 350--850 nm were extracted, background-subtracted, and wavelength-calibrated using IRAF. Corrections accounted for the wavelength-dependent quantum efficiencies of Sony IMX249 and IMX273 detectors and atmospheric attenuation as a function of observing geometry. The corrected spectra were decomposed into Fe, Mg, and Na components using selected atomic transitions, temperature-dependent emissivities, and pseudo-Voigt line profiles. Integrated Fe~I-15, Mg~I-2, and Na~I-1 intensities were compared in a ternary diagram. Most spectra overlap with or lie near the normal-meteor distribution in reference samples, while some extend toward Fe-rich or Na-rich regions. The most Fe-dominated event assigns approximately 81\% of the summed emission to Fe~I-15. These ratios characterize relative emission, not elemental abundances or bulk composition. Combined with trajectory and photometric data, spectral classification may help constrain plausible material properties in dark-flight models and refine predicted meteorite search areas.

(a) Correction curves calculated for meteor altitudes between 20 and 200 km at a fixed apparent elevation of $20^{\circ}$. title: MACE: Multigroup-Multiangle Integrated Thermal Compton Scattering Kernel
authors: Itamar Giron, Menahem Krief, Elad Steinberg
abstract: We present a comprehensive set of accurate Compton-scattering tables for use in multigroup, multiangle radiation-transport calculations. The tables contain the exact thermal Compton kernel integrated over incident-energy groups, scattered-energy groups, and angular bins. To generate them, we develop a deterministic integration method in which the pointwise kernel is evaluated with a robust numerical treatment that remains accurate across challenging regions of parameter space. The multidimensional integrals are computed using nested quadratures whose panels adapt to the Compton recoil ridge, its thermal broadening, and the nearly elastic forward-scattering boundary layer. We validate the tabulated results against published kernel profiles, angular and energy moments, mean free paths, multigroup redistribution data, and an independent Monte Carlo estimator. The resulting tables provide the radiation-transport community with accurate, reproducible, and readily usable Compton redistribution matrices and angular moments.
comments: 36 pages, 34 figures, 3 tables. Submitted to ApJS. Code: this https URL ; pre-computed scattering matrices: this https URL

title: Beyond dust in local cosmography: perturbative Vlasov predictions
authors: Chris Clarkson, Roy Maartens
abstract: The dust approximation used in cosmography neglects the velocity dispersion generated during structure formation. This dispersion produces isotropic and anisotropic pressure, whose gradients accelerate the mean matter flow even though individual particles follow geodesics. The acceleration introduces an intrinsic dipole into the local distance-redshift relation. We calculate this dipole and the accompanying changes in expansion and shear using linear Vlasov perturbation theory about an FLRW background, with a mean dispersion history motivated by halo estimates. The assumed FLRW background prevents an independent test of the cosmological principle; the numerical predictions also depend on the adopted LCDM cosmology. Pressure also changes the growth of structure, modifying the shear and the spatial gradients that govern how the distance anisotropy varies with redshift. The largest correction at the lowest order in redshift is to the shear, while changes in the expansion gradient can produce a larger dipole at the next order. The resulting intrinsic dipole is far smaller than the observed low-redshift dipole, whose behaviour nearest the observer is dominated by motion between the matter and CMB frames.
comments: 31 pages, with 8 figures

title: Companions of Hot Jupiters: two decades of radial velocity monitoring with CORALIE
authors: Léna Parc, João P. Faria, François Bouchy, Jana Baron, Siddharth Bhatnagar, Nicolas Billot, Yann Carteret, Guillaume Chaverot, Adrien Deline, Jean-Baptiste Delisle, Pedro Figueira, Emile Fontanet, Nathan C. Hara, Mathilde Houelle, Maxime Marmier, Marion Neveu-VanMalle, Louise D. Nielsen, Javiera Rey, Damien Ségransan, Manu Stalport, Stéphane Udry
abstract: Hot Jupiters are thought to form through multiple pathways, some of which can leave observable signatures in the architecture of their planetary systems. Massive outer companions, in particular, can provide important constraints on the dynamical histories of hot Jupiters. We aim to characterize the occurrence rate and orbital properties of additional giant companions in hot Jupiter systems, and to investigate whether these companions provide evidence for the role of dynamical interactions in shaping the hot Jupiter population. We perform a homogeneous long-term radial-velocity analysis of 147 WASP hot Jupiter systems observed with the CORALIE spectrograph between 2007 and 2025. We identify or refine 13 outer giant companions and use individual radial-velocity posteriors within a Bayesian occurrence-rate framework to measure the frequency of giant companions over orbital periods of 10--6250 days. The occurrence rate of additional giant companions increases strongly with orbital period, from {2}lt;0.01$ and 0.02 at 10--50 and 50--250 days to 0.05 and 0.17 at 250--1250 and 1250--6250 days, respectively, in agreement with the giant-planet occurrence of the general FGK population and with previous estimates of outer companions to hot Jupiters. Hot Jupiters with detected companions have longer orbital periods and higher eccentricities than those without. We also find that companion eccentricity decreases with hot Jupiter period, and that the companion-to-hot-Jupiter mass ratio increases with period ratio, both consistent with expectations from high-eccentricity migration (HEM). Our results support HEM as the mechanism shaping hot Jupiters with outer companions. Combining long-baseline radial velocities with future Gaia astrometry will further constrain companion masses, mutual inclinations, and dynamical histories.
comments: 17 pages, 10 figures. Accepted for publication in A&A

title: Mode power and stability in radial post-AGB pulsations
authors: Jan Zalewski
abstract: We examine the relation between mode power and excitation rate for radial pulsations along a sequence of high-luminosity post-AGB envelope models. The net thermodynamic exchange power, including boundary contributions, is compared with the excitation rate and the inertia, compression and horizontal area deformation norms entering the balance relation. We find that positive net exchange power can accompany damping, while negative net exchange power can accompany excitation. Along an individual mode sequence, the power may reverse sign repeatedly without a change of stability. These reversals are associated with changes in the sign of the effective norm. Including the compression contribution in the pressure-force power does not remove this behaviour and can extend the intervals of sign disagreement. Thus, although spatial exchange integrals identify positive and negative contributions to the modal power, the sign of the global power alone does not generally determine mode stability.
comments: 13 pages, 5 figures

title: IMF-aware N-body forward modelling of membership selection functions for young open clusters
authors: Yue-Yue Shen, Chao Liu, Zepeng Zheng, Long Wang, Xiaoying Pang, Bo Zhang, Hao Tian, Yang Xiang
abstract: We present an IMF-aware N-body forward-modelling framework, in which the stellar initial mass function (IMF) is an explicit input, to quantify the membership selection functions of open clusters, namely completeness and contamination as functions of magnitude. Accurate derivation of the IMF requires correcting for these selection effects, which otherwise distort the inferred present-day mass function. Our framework simulates clusters with IMF slopes $\alpha_2 = -2.7, -2.3, -1.9$, converts them into synthetic Gaia observations, adds mock field populations, and recovers members with HDBSCAN to mimic observational membership selection. Applying this framework to 35 young open clusters (ages $\lesssim100$ Myr, distances $\lesssim600$ pc), we find declining completeness towards the faint limit; older, more expanded, and more diffuse models have lower completeness and higher contamination. For a given cluster, models with flatter IMFs yield modestly but systematically lower global completeness and higher contamination, despite initial cluster masses calibrated to the same observed member count. These models undergo more stellar evolution mass loss and expand more, resulting in lower projected stellar densities; their lower completeness is consistent with more diffuse clusters being harder to separate from field stars. Corrections derived from a mismatched IMF largely recover the total star counts but leave a larger distortion in the shape of the present-day luminosity function than those derived with the correct IMF. Because membership recovery is tied to a cluster's structural evolution and the specific membership algorithm used, our findings emphasize that selection functions should be inferred jointly with the IMF rather than assumed in advance.
comments: 20 pages, 8 figures, 2 tables. Under revision at MNRAS

title: Activity Cycles in Solar-Type Stars
authors: P. D. Colombo, C.A. Peralta, A. P. Buccino, C. G. Oviedo, R. Ibañez Bustos, C. F. Martinez, M. Flores Trivigno, F. Minotti, P. Mauas
abstract: Systematic observational studies, mainly focused on solar-type stars in the F to early K range, have detected magnetic activity cycles analogous to the solar one. When analyzing the relationship between the length of these cycles and stellar rotation rate, a non-monotonic dependence is observed. Activity periods are discretely distributed into two distinct branches: inactive and active. Intriguingly, some stars with rotation rates faster than the Sun exhibit two coexisting activity cycles, with periods simultaneously falling on both the inactive and active branches. In this work, we analyze the time series of the Mount Wilson index of a set of 44 stars, covering a range of rotation periods (sub-solar, solar, and super-solar), to identify single or double activity cycles. We detected activity cycles in 19 of the analyzed stars, with 7 of these exhibiting double-cycle behavior. In a complementary approach, we also analyze the activity cycles simulated for identical solar twins with rotation periods both shorter and longer than the Sun.
comments: Accepted in Proc. IAUS 400

title: Ultraviolet accretion continua reveal a transition in T Tauri magnetic topology
authors: Ana I Gomez de Castro
abstract: Magnetic fields regulate accretion in T Tauri stars (TTSs) and evolve as radiative cores emerge during pre-main-sequence contraction. Stars above ~0.35-0.5 Msun transition from fully convective to partially convective interiors, a change associated with increasingly complex magnetic topologies and evolving dynamo behaviour. Because accretion flows are magnetically channelled, this evolution is expected to modify ultraviolet (UV) accretion diagnostics, although observational evidence has remained limited. We identify a transition in the UV continuum properties of TTSs using archival International Ultraviolet Explorer observations, complemented by recent spectra from the Hubble Space Telescope ULLYSES survey. An empirical UV photospheric sequence constructed from G-M main-sequence stars shows that late K-M TTSs broadly follow standard photosphere-plus-shock model predictions, whereas G-K5 stars display systematically lower F270/F303 continuum flux ratios (flux at 270 nm relative to 303 nm). Statistical analysis shows that transition models describe the observations significantly better than a single continuous trend, locating the transition near spectral type K5-K6, with its precise location limited by spectral-classification uncertainties, and consistent with the fully convective boundary. Comparison with photosphere-plus-shock models further shows that, while the late-type population is broadly encompassed by the parameter space sampled by the adopted models, the warmer stars extend systematically beyond it in this UV diagnostic. We interpret this transition as evidence for a change in magnetospheric accretion associated with the evolution of magnetic topology across the radiative-core boundary, resulting in a corresponding change in the emergent UV continuum.
comments: Astrophysical Journal Letters, accepted (4 figures)

title: Statistical Analysis of Neutron Star Cooling: Implications for the Nuclear Equation of State and Nucleon Pairing
authors: Afonso Ávila, Ricardo Z. Ferreira, Violetta Sagun
abstract: We perform a statistical analysis of the thermal evolution of isolated neutron stars by confronting theoretical cooling curves with luminosity-age measurements for 24 sources. For each object, we explore five purely nucleonic equations of state (APR4, FSU2R, DD2, IST, and NL3$\omega\rho$) combined with representative models of neutron superfluidity and proton superconductivity, while varying the gravitational mass and envelope composition. The analysis spans approximately $10^5$ cooling curves. Within this framework, we find that only the NL3$\omega\rho$ equation of state and, to a lesser extent, IST, both including neutron triplet pairing, provide an overall satisfactory description of the data. The remaining equations of state are in significant tension with the observations. These results demonstrate that NS cooling provides complementary constraints on dense matter, alongside nuclear structure, global NS observables, and gravitational-wave observations, while probing the interplay between the EoS and nucleon pairing.
comments: 12 pages, 6 figures, 4 tables

title: Dynamical response of a protoplanetary disk to an FU Ori-type outburst
authors: Roman Zolotarev, Yaroslav Pavlyuchenkov, Vitaly Akimkin
abstract: Episodic accretion events onto young stars can significantly change the global structure of their surrounding protoplanetary disks. Using radiation hydrodynamical simulations with the HURAKAN code, we study the response of the outer passive disk to a powerful FU Ori-type outburst. Disk heating initiates a factor-of-two increase in the vertical scale-height, which develops on a local keplerian timescale. This effectively launches an outward travelling wave with a bump whose radial position changes with time as $r_{b}\sim t^{2/3}$. After the outburst ends, new waves are launched as the disk structure re-equilibrates toward a quiescent state. The vertical expansion of the disk introduces significant time-variable extinction of the central source emission. Disks with inclinations in the range $40^{\circ}<i<60^{\circ}$ go from weakly ($A_{V}<1$) to a strongly embedded state ($A_{V}\sim10^2$), with the extinction decaying on a $\sim10^2$ yr timescale after the outburst. A fingerprint of the outburst-launched shadowing wave is a long-lived drop or a transient dip in the luminosity curve occurring several years after the outburst begins. This apparent luminosity variation is relatively large, up to $1^m-3^m$ in the V band, and is not related to the intrinsic accretion variability.
comments: Accepted for publication in The Astrophysical Journal

title: Connecting galaxy structure, quenching, and halo environments during cosmic noon
authors: Ziwen Zhang, Cheng Jia, Huiyuan Wang, Enci Wang, Yangyao Chen, Houjun Mo, Xiong Luo, Cheqiu Lyu, Jie Song
abstract: The connection between galaxy structure, star formation activity, and large-scale environments provides important insights into the evolution of massive galaxies. However, the relative importance of different galaxy properties in predicting quenching and the environmental dependence of structurally distinct galaxy populations remain poorly constrained at cosmic noon ($1\leq z<3$). In this work, we investigate massive galaxies with $\log M_*/{\rm M}_{\odot}>10.5$ at $1\leq z<3$ using deep JWST/NIRCam imaging from the COSMOS-Web survey, combining measurements of central stellar mass surface density ($\Sigma_1$), star formation activity, and galaxy clustering. We find that $\Sigma_1$ is the most informative predictor of quenching among the considered properties, including stellar mass, effective radius, formation redshift, and local overdensity. The quenched fraction shows a strong dependence on $\Sigma_1$, increasing rapidly above a characteristic $\Sigma_1$. We further show that compact quenched galaxies exhibit a tendency toward stronger clustering than compact and extended star-forming galaxies, while compact and extended star-forming galaxies show similar clustering properties. These results highlight the importance of $\Sigma_1$ in tracing quenching and reveal that structural diversity among star-forming galaxies is not strongly reflected in their large-scale environments, providing new constraints on the interplay between galaxy structure, quenching, and halo environments during cosmic noon.

title: Hyperonic Direct-Urca Neutrino Emission with Lattice-QCD-Informed Form Factors
authors: Andreas Konstantinou
abstract: We investigate the sensitivity of direct-Urca neutrino emission in hyperonic neutron-star matter to the structure and momentum dependence of baryonic transition form factors. Using the zero-temperature FSU2H relativistic mean-field equation of state, we derive the relativistic emissivity for general spin-$1/2$ baryon transitions with the complete six form-factor contribution. We compare conventional static flavor-SU(3) couplings with vacuum lattice-QCD-informed form factors, using direct lattice vacuum input for $n\rightarrow p$ and $\Lambda\rightarrow p$ and a hybrid construction for the remaining hyperonic channels. Evaluating the latter both at $q^2=0$ and at the kinetic momentum transfer sampled at the Fermi surfaces separates changes in the zero-momentum couplings from momentum-transfer effects. The sensitivity is strongly channel dependent. The nucleonic transition probes $q^2\simeq0$ and is only weakly affected, whereas hyperonic channels can sample substantially larger momentum transfers and receive correspondingly larger corrections. These modifications propagate to the integrated neutrino luminosity of stellar configurations. Our results estimate the possible scale of the sensitivity coming from momentum transfer dependence, absent from static-coupling treatments and motivate future first-principles studies of baryonic weak currents in dense matter.

figs.cap: Density dependence of the FSU2H composition, direct-Urca kinematics, and form-factor sensitivity of the $\Lambda\rightarrow p$ channel. Panel (d) shows $Q_{\Lambda p,e}+Q_{\Lambda p,\mu}$ while progressively introducing the $q_{F}^{2}$ dependence of the six directly calculated $\Lambda\rightarrow p$ form factors. The vertical dashed line denotes the central density of the maximum-mass stable FSU2H star. The shaded region is not reached by stable stellar configurations.

Dashed curves denote the static flavor-SU(3) reference evaluated at $q^{2}=0$, while solid curves use the direct or hybrid lattice-informed form factors evaluated at the kinetic Fermi-surface transfer $q_{F}^{2}$. title: The Next Generation Virgo Cluster Survey (NGVS). XXIX. Demography of Nuclear Star Clusters
authors: Max M. Kurzner, Patrick Côté, Laura Ferrarese, Chelsea Spengler, Eric W. Peng, Rubén Sánchez-Janssen, Joel C. Roediger, Kaixiang Wang, Chengze Liu, Sungsoon Lim, Matthew A. Taylor, Eleanore B. Todd, Patrick R. Durrell, Elisa Toloba, Puragra Guhathakurta, J. Christopher Mihos, John P. Blakeslee, Hong-Xin Zhang
abstract: Nuclear star clusters (NSCs) provide insights into processes shaping galaxy cores. We use deep $u^*giz$ CFHT imaging from the Next Generation Virgo Cluster Survey (NGVS) to study NSCs in Virgo cluster galaxies. Our parent sample consists of 3680 certain, likely or possible cluster members spanning more than six orders of magnitude in stellar mass. Using a self-consistent classification framework, we identify 1144 candidate nucleated galaxies: 804 high-confidence NSCs and 340 lower-confidence candidates. This is the largest and most uniform NSC catalog for any environment studied to date. We explore the nucleation fraction, $f_{\rm nuc}$, as a function of stellar mass, morphology and environment. Consistent with previous studies, we find stellar mass a key factor driving nucleation probability. However, host-galaxy morphology is also important, with the peak of the $f_{\rm nuc}$ distribution occurring at progressively lower masses as one moves from later to earlier morphological types. We interpret this shift as evidence that the more extended structures of late-type galaxies reduce the efficiency of GC inspiral at fixed stellar mass, while gas-rich secular processes and central star formation may contribute increasingly to NSC growth at higher masses. Environment plays a smaller role, with only a slight enhancement in high-density regions. We characterize the nonlinear relationship between NSC stellar mass and host-galaxy mass, and assess the role of selection effects. We conclude that NSC formation is best explained by a hybrid scenario, with inspiraling star clusters and in situ star formation contributing, and their relative importance dictated primarily by galaxy mass.
comments: 47 pages, 27 figures, 3 tables, Accepted to ApJ

title: Characterization of integrating-sphere systematic effects for photon calibration of the KAGRA gravitational wave detector
authors: Shingo Hido, Misato Onishi, Shinji Miyoki, Takahiro Sawada, Takahiro Yamamoto, Takayuki Tomaru, Yoshiki Moriwaki, Dan Chen
abstract: Photon calibration (Pcal) systems are essential for accurately reconstructing gravitational-wave strain in laser interferometric detectors. In the KAGRA Pcal system, the laser power applied to the end test mass is measured using integrating-sphere power sensors. During the first part of the fourth observing run (O4a), repeated calibration measurements showed scatter larger than expected from the uncertainties assigned to individual measurements. Although this excess scatter was empirically reflected in the previously reported calibration uncertainties, its physical origin was not identified. In this study, we experimentally characterize the response of the integrating spheres used in the KAGRA calibration chain with respect to three incident-beam conditions: incidence angle, polarization, and beam position. Based on these measurements and the reproducibility of the integrating-sphere placement in each calibration configuration, we evaluate the corresponding systematic uncertainties and explicitly incorporate them into the uncertainty model for the O4a Pcal-X calibration measurements. The inclusion of these previously unmodeled effects substantially improves the consistency between the estimated uncertainties and the observed scatter, particularly for calibration parameters measured at the KAGRA end station, where the reduced chi-square values decrease from values as large as $10^3$ to values of order unity to several. These results indicate that variations in the incident-beam conditions of integrating-sphere power sensors account for a substantial part of the previously unexplained scatter and establish a more physically motivated framework for evaluating Pcal laser-power calibration uncertainty. They also provide a basis for future reduction of the calibration uncertainty through improved control of the incident-beam conditions.
comments: 20 pages, 15 figures

title: Reading Between the Lines: How Much Information Remains After Fitting a Stellar Spectrum?
authors: Sven Buder, Tomasz Różánski
abstract: What if we could model 100% of a stellar spectrum? Modern surveys infer stellar properties by comparing observed spectra with synthetic models, yet even the best fits leave structured residuals. We analyse 7087 GALAH survey spectra and ask what information remains after subtracting each best-fitting model. Across 13927 pixels, 4.5% of residuals exceed $3\sigma$, far above 0.3% expected from Gaussian noise. We map the amplitude, significance, sign, and recurrence of these residuals and identify 380 significant regions. Comparison with stellar atlases, line lists, diffuse interstellar bands, and sky diagnostics links most regions to plausible causes: 62% are candidate line-strength or line-profile mismatches, while others trace missing or unidentified lines, interstellar absorption, sky emission, or broader reduction structure. We then train data-driven models on the residual spectra themselves. Residual-only models recover $T_\mathrm{eff}$ to 80-150 K and [Fe/H] to 0.059-0.086 dex, depending on sample quality, and retain weaker, partly indirect information about elemental abundances. Extinction-related coefficients recover the strongest known interstellar features, whereas chromospheric activity leaves plausible Balmer-line signatures but is not recovered robustly out of sample. Most strikingly, the residual flux in 6% of wavelength pixels that were synthesised but excluded from the GALAH DR4 optimisation recovers stellar labels almost as well as the full residual spectrum and better than the remaining 94% alone. Residuals are therefore not merely imperfections to discard: they map missing line data, incomplete physics, unfitted astrophysical components, and observational systematics. Reading between the lines turns one spectroscopist's trash into another one's treasure, and provides a practical route towards extracting more of the information already present in stellar spectra.
comments: 21 pages, 14 figures; submitted to the Open Journal of Astrophysics; code at this https URL comments welcome

title: Constraints on the Progenitor of SN 2023bee from its Nebular-Phase Spectra
authors: Sophie von Coelln, Qinan Wang, Matthew R. Siebert, Ping Chen, Armin Rest, Luc Dessart, Yossef Zenati, Georgios Dimitriadis, Katie Auchettl, Siyuan Chen, Kyle W. Davis, Thomas de Boer, Ryan J. Foley, Avishay Gal-Yam, Willem B. Hoogendam, Mark E. Huber, Luca Izzo, Charles D. Kilpatrick, Chien-Cheng Lin, Chang Liu, Thomas Bernard Lowe, Gautham Narayan, César Rojas-Bravo, Aidan Sedgewick, Koji Shukawa, Richard J. Wainscoat
abstract: We present late-time photometry (~100-400 days after peak) and nebular-phase optical/NIR spectroscopy (100-360 days) of the Type Ia supernova (SN Ia) SN 2023bee. This SN Ia was observed TESS immediately before and after explosion and showed a relatively weak early excess light-curve feature detected in multiple UV and optical bands. Possible explanations for this early excess feature include interaction between the SN ejecta and a non-degenerate companion, or the decay of radioactive isotopes synthesized near the ejecta surface in a sub-$\text{M}_\text{Ch}$ double-detonation scenario. However, the degeneracies and incompleteness of existing models have so far prevented a definitive conclusion about its progenitor system. Nebular-phase spectra provide a complementary probe of SN Ia progenitors by constraining stripped H/He-rich material and iron-group abundances sensitive to the progenitor white dwarf density. We report the non-detection of narrow H/He features in nebular phase optical/NIR spectra of SN 2023bee, placing upper limits of $m^{\text{stripped}}_\text{H}\lesssim5.0\times10^{-3}\text{ M}_\odot$ and $m_\text{He}^{\text{stripped}}\lesssim1.2\times10^{-4}\text{ M}_\odot$. These limits strongly disfavor a non-degenerate companion and suggest that companion interaction is unlikely to explain the early excess of SN 2023bee. We also performed line-diagnostic measurements on the 7200 Åcomplex using multi-Gaussian fitting and continuum estimation, with the inferred velocities validated against NIR spectrum at the similar phase. The resulting low Ni-to-Fe mass ratio, $m_\text{Ni}/m_\text{Fe}\lesssim 0.06$, is broadly consistent with a sub-$M_{\text{Ch}}$ double-detonation progenitor system.
comments: 16 pages, 6 figures; submitted to ApJ

title: Plate-YOLO: An End-to-End Object Detection Framework for Robust Astrometric Registration of Historical Plates
authors: Quanfeng Xu, Zhengjun Shang, Shiyin Shen, Yong Yu, Mingyang Ma, Zhenghong Tang, Meiting Yang, Jing Yang, Jianhai Zhao
abstract: Historical astronomical plates provide a long temporal baseline for time-domain astrophysics, but degradation and structural artifacts can hinder automated astrometric calibration. We present Plate-YOLO, a framework that combines source detection and stellar classification in one detector and supplies source catalogs to a separate astrometric solver. The detector adapts YOLOv5 with Space-to-Depth feature rearrangement, SimAM attention, a high-resolution P2 head, and a Normalized Wasserstein Distance loss for small bounding boxes. A Gaia-guided fine-tuning procedure uses initially solved plates to construct labels for a new archive. On 150 UBAI plates for which the conventional pipeline had failed, the Chinese-trained model solved 40 plates, and target-archive fine-tuning recovered a further 106, giving an overall recovery rate of 146/150 (97.3%). In the reported hardware configuration, source extraction took 6.61 s per plate for Plate-YOLO and 16.73 s for SExtractor. These results demonstrate the practical value of adapting source detection to degraded historical plates.
comments: 14 pages, 6 figures, accepted for publication in The Astronomical Journal

title: Velocity-resolved Ionization Mapping of the Broad-line Region. II. Signatures of Eccentric Broad-line Regions from a Quantitative Photoionization-Based Model
authors: Jiancheng Wu, Hai-Cheng Feng, Sha-Sha Li, Qingwen Wu, Xinwu Cao
abstract: Velocity-resolved reverberation mapping (RM) is one of the most powerful tools for probing the geometry and kinematics of the broad-line region in active galactic nuclei. However, its interpretation may be non-unique, as similar velocity-delay signatures can arise from different combinations of BLR geometry and kinematics. To address this degeneracy, this series of studies develops velocity-resolved ionization mapping (IM) as a complementary technique. In this second paper of the series, we construct photoionization-based BLR models to quantitatively demonstrate the diagnostic power of the joint RM+IM framework. We calculate local \ha\ and \hb\ emissivities with Cloudy, couple them with disk-like BLR models, and generate synthetic velocity-dependent line fluxes, lags, and Balmer decrements. The model reproduces the observed anti-correlation between the integrated BD and the incident ionizing continuum, with scatter naturally introduced by reverberation delays. We show that a virialized elliptical BLR can produce diverse velocity-delay maps and velocity-resolved lags that mimic RM signatures commonly attributed to virialized motion, inflow, or outflow. In contrast, the velocity-resolved BD is sensitive to the symmetry of the BLR gas distribution, providing a key diagnostic for distinguishing eccentric geometry from non-virial motions. Through proof-of-concept comparisons with one double-peaked and one single-peaked AGN, we show that an elliptical-disk BLR can simultaneously reproduce the observed line profiles, velocity-resolved lags, and velocity-resolved BDs. These results provide a quantitative basis for IM, support the presence of eccentric BLR structures in AGNs, and demonstrate the potential of joint RM+IM analyses to break the BLR geometry-kinematics degeneracy.

title: The DARWIN Project: Cosmological Simulations of Galaxy Formation down to Dwarf Scales in Diverse Environments
authors: Jaehyun Lee, Kyungwon Chun, Taysun Kimm, Yonghwi Kim, Jihye Shin, Ena Choi, Sungwook E. Hong, Myoungwon Jeon, Hannah Jhee, Hyeonyong Kim, Ji-hoon Kim, Juhan Kim, Oh-Kyoung Kwon, Hyunmi Song, Yohan Dubois, Ji-Hoon Ha, Daniel Han, San Han, Jun Yong Park, Christophe Pichon
abstract: We present the DARWIN project, a suite of cosmological simulations with RAMSES to study dwarf-galaxy formation and evolution across diverse environments. DARWIN-1 is a full-box simulation in a cubic volume of $(65.5\,{\rm cMpc})^3$ with a minimum cell size of 500pc, while DARWIN-2 comprises zoom-in simulations of 24 field regions and a Milky Way analog connected to a filament, reaching 62.5pc resolution. The simulations employ baryonic physics tailored to their aims. For DARWIN-2, we include radiative transfer in three photon energy bands to trace hydrogen and helium ionization. DARWIN-1 reproduces the cosmic star formation rate density and galaxy stellar mass functions reasonably well at $z>1$. Both simulations broadly reproduce observed stellar mass-halo mass relations, chemical abundances, star-formation surface densities, and black hole-galaxy scaling relations. At lower redshift, DARWIN-1 shows an excess in the number density of massive galaxies, although the inferred stellar content of massive halos depends on the definition of galaxy stellar mass. Other systematic differences arise from spatial resolution, feedback efficiency, and environmental selection. To facilitate comparison with observations, we generate mock images using the radiative transfer codes SKIRT and Powderday. We also explore a machine-learning approach to mitigate resolution-driven biases in the dwarf galaxy properties of DARWIN-1 using the higher-resolution DARWIN-2 simulations. The DARWIN simulation suite therefore provides a comprehensive numerical framework for studying the formation, evolution, and internal physics of dwarf galaxies in a cosmological context.
comments: 33 pages, 18 figures, submitted to ApJ, any comments welcome

title: A Morphology-Based Cross-Tracer Ratio for Robust BAO Tests
authors: Paula S. Ferreira, Carlos A. P. Bengaly, Renyue Cen
abstract: We use the Cross-Tracer Clustering Ratio (CTCR) acoustic response estimator, a new probe of morphology-dependent galaxy clustering in photometric surveys. CTCR is the ratio of the auto-power spectrum of early-type galaxies (ETGs) to their cross-power spectrum with late-type galaxies (LTGs). In the matched-kernel deterministic linear-bias limit the CTCR cancels the complete projected matter spectrum, including the baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) wiggles, leaving only the relative linear bias. This makes the ratio uniquely sensitive to physics beyond deterministic linear bias: any residual acoustic structure in the CTCR must arise from a difference between the normalised non-linear responses of the two tracers. We, for the first time, exploit this property to model the measured ratio as a smooth scale-dependent baseline multiplied by a scale-dependent acoustic template, and constrain the amplitude $A_{\rm morph}$ of the differential acoustic response jointly with the BAO dilation parameter $\alpha$. Applying the estimator to nine bins of the DESI Legacy Survey Data Release 8 spanning $0.1 < z < 0.9$, we obtain$\alpha = 0.9997 \pm 0.0383$, consistent with the Planck 2018 $\Lambda$CDM prediction, and $A_{\rm morph} = 0.369 \pm 0.307$, consistent with zero. A Bayesian model comparison yields at most a 2.6$\sigma$ preference for the acoustic template over a smooth-only baseline. The estimator is model-independent, requires no external calibration of the absolute bias, and is directly applicable to the wide-field imaging surveys that will define the next decade of cosmology. It offers a new route to testing halo occupation and assembly-bias models, and an independent, systematics-robust cross-check of BAO measurements from spectroscopic surveys.

The matched configuration (black, drawn on top) uses identical kernels for both tracers with $\sigma_{z}=0.05$. The three mismatch scenarios are a width mismatch (ETG $\sigma_{z}=0.03$, LTG $\sigma_{z}=0.08$, blue), a centre mismatch (LTG displaced by $\Delta z=+0.05$, orange), and a combined mismatch (ETG at $\Delta z=-0.05$ with $\sigma_{z}=0.03$, LTG at $\Delta z=+0.05$ with $\sigma_{z}=0.08$, red). The mismatched cases show the same acoustic structure but with an additional smooth broadband offset that grows toward low $\ell$ and that is largest for the combined scenario. This smooth residual is the systematic that the sigmoid baseline of Eq. (33) is designed to absorb, and it illustrates why bins with strongly mismatched kernels cannot be used for BAO extraction.
